analysis.title: Squeeze-&-Chase, Not Rotation: Goldman Spots One Major Investor Class Conspicuously Absent From Nasdaq Record Highs
key_insights: Nasdaq 100 closed at a record high. The index rose 2.9% from Sep 29 to Oct 6, versus the S&P +1.9% and the Russell 2000 +0.8%. Nasdaq futures aggregate open interest rose a net $8.9B over the same span.

GS's Robert Quinn argues the open interest build is not mostly new longs. Funding data showed simultaneous short selling, and sponsorship from asset managers, the largest non-dealer cohort, remained questionable.

Nasdaq 3-month funding cheapened in outright terms and moved sideways relative to the S&P. Quinn reads this as outright shorts and/or hedging fueling some of the OI builds, since funding normally richens when longs pile in.

Open interest rose in 3 of the 5 sessions for a net $8.9B, with the largest upticks on Oct 2 and Oct 5 alongside price strength. Aggregate OI ran to roughly 325,000+ contracts in mid-September, fell to about 271,000 around the September quarterly expiry, and rebounded only to the mid-280,000s (the article's read of the GS chart).
GS AI Leaders basket rose 6.4% and the Broad AI basket 5.6% over the period, helped by significant infrastructure agreements. The AI baskets more than doubled the Nasdaq's gain.

Asset manager gross longs have generally declined since a nominal max on Jun 2. Their correlation between gross long changes (in contracts) and price was nil as of the Sep 29 Commitment of Traders update. The article reads the rolling 6-month correlation as about 0.45 in May-July and roughly 0.05 or less now.
In dollar terms, asset manager gross longs peaked above $70B in early June and were around $66B by late September (article's read of the chart), while the Nasdaq made new records.

The article ties this to Quinn's S&P work: asset managers sold $11.7B of S&P futures in the week to Sep 29, part of a $63.7B non-dealer exodus since mid-August. Quinn's earlier read was that S&P futures flows arguably remained bearish.
The article names fast money as the marginal buyer. Bloomberg's Simon White noted speculators lifted their Nasdaq futures net long to near decade highs (2017 highs) on Sep 28.

GS cash desk mid-day color on Oct 8: long-only clients were '-25% better for sale' with massive sell skews across macro products and tech names. Tuesday's close had asset manager and hedge fund flows skewed to buy, but the desk called them muted.

AI funding is shifting toward debt. The FT reported SpaceX wants to raise $40B (about $10B bank loans, $30B IG debt) to pay for its Nvidia order, reportedly through an Apollo-backed SPV collateralized by NVDA chips. GS's Rich Privorotsky said more leverage in the AI ecosystem is not what the market wants to hear.

GS's Edoardo Greco flagged competition for capital into 2027: US Treasury net new issuance of $1tn versus GS forecasting $420B of gross AI-related debt issuance. GS's Noah Gurney noted AI hyperscaler credit spreads opened 2-3bps wider on the SpaceX financing reports.

GS's Shawn Tuteja, an AI/semis bull at the end of August, now says the Tech/AI asymmetry has shifted, macro is unequivocally more difficult, and positioning in AI and large-cap tech is no longer a tailwind. Since Aug 27, SPX is +1.28% while the S&P ex-AI names index (SPXXAI) is -5.19%.
Prime book positioning: Mag 7 net exposure is near 22% of total US exposure, the highest since the start of 2022, and long levered semis ETFs hold about $115B.

Breadth is weak. The Russell underperformed the NDX for the 4th straight day and 17 of the last 20 sessions. GS's Bartlett attributed the NDX breakout to clean positioning (HF nets approaching a 5-year low), covering of macro products/hedges, and concentration into Tech/AI, with breadth at its lowest since 2000.

Futures slid from Tuesday's record as Iran stepped up tanker attacks in Hormuz and the 30Y yield hit a 2002 high. Nasdaq 100 futures retested the prior day's lows and SpaceX shares fell after the chip-loan report.

The article's bull counterpoint from Tuteja: US Fundamental L/S nets are in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback, and clients are seen wanting to buy around 7,400 on the S&P, which should cushion dips.

Next tells are today's 30Y auction and Friday's CFTC Commitment of Traders release (data through Tuesday's close). Flat asset manager gross longs in a record-high week would confirm Quinn's skepticism.

sector_views.rationale: Tuteja says the Tech/AI asymmetry has shifted and positioning in AI and large-cap tech is no longer a tailwind. Asset managers are not sponsoring the Nasdaq rally, and AI buildout is increasingly debt-funded.
The Russell has lagged the NDX in 17 of the last 20 sessions as small caps bear the brunt of the rates pain.

macro_indicators.interpretation: High yields make GPU-collateralized AI debt a less attractive profile for long-only money to chase.
Hit alongside Iran tanker attacks in Hormuz and pressured futures from Tuesday's record.
Competes with a GS-forecast $420B of gross AI-related debt issuance for capital.

risk_factors: Asset managers are not sponsoring the Nasdaq rally, leaving it dependent on fast money, short covering and levered ETF flows.
Increasing debt financing of AI buildout, including chip-collateralized loans, with 10Y yields above 5%.
Competition for capital: $1tn net Treasury issuance versus $420B of expected gross AI-related debt issuance.
Extreme index concentration and breadth at its lowest since 2000.
Geopolitical escalation in Hormuz and the 30Y yield at a 2002 high.
Heavy prime-book Mag 7 exposure and levered semis ETF holdings could amplify a reversal.

tension_points.bull_case: Overall positioning is light: US Fundamental L/S nets are in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback and clients are seen wanting to buy around ~7,400 on the S&P, which should cushion dips.
tension_points.bear_case: Asset manager longs are below their June peak with price correlation near nil, funding cheapened as OI rose, marginal buyers are fast money and levered ETFs, and breadth is the worst since 2000.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Friday's CFTC Commitment of Traders release: if asset manager gross longs do not rise in a week the Nasdaq made new highs, the skeptical read is confirmed. A rise in asset manager length would challenge it.
